the relationship between lung function (measured as forced vital capacity [FVC]) and cardiovascular disease risk is partially explained by the presence of elevated levels of inflammation-sensitive proteins (fibrinogen, α1-antitripsin, haptogloin, cerulopasmin, and orsomucoid).
the relationship between lung function and cardiovascular disease risk is partly explained by inflammation-sensitive plasma proteins, but that other mechanisms are also involved.
